notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Synchronization between environments and destinations is one of the primary user pains and should be a first-class object in the product.

notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Milestone 2 must introduce a stable target-plugin contract. Vercel is the first implementation, not a provider-specific path in core. External third-party plugin loading is deferred; M2 ships only first-party plugins bundled with the product.

notes.author: human:product-owner
notes.text: Roadmap renumbered after splitting secure core from runtime secrets; now M3.

problem: Teams cannot easily see which secret version is active across local development, CI, preview, staging and production destinations.
scope: Introduce a provider-neutral SyncBinding and desired-state reconciliation model.

Define a stable SecretTargetPlugin contract with capability discovery, connection validation, push/delete operations where supported, target inspection where supported and provider-specific scope mapping.
Keep sync engine responsibilities in core: desired version, scheduling/retry, state transitions and audit.
Keep provider responsibilities inside plugins: authentication, API calls, environment/scope mapping and capability reporting.
Implement Vercel as the first first-party target plugin.
Render generic target configuration from plugin metadata/config schema where practical.
Do not load arbitrary npm/community plugins in-process in this milestone.
title: Milestone 3: pluggable target synchronization with Vercel
validation: The Vercel implementation uses only the target-plugin contract; core synchronization code contains no Vercel-specific branching.
A secret version can be bound to a Vercel project/environment and synchronized from the source of truth.
Each binding reports pending, synced or failed state plus last attempt and error metadata.
Adding a second first-party target can be done by implementing the plugin contract without changing the reconciliation domain model.
Plugin capabilities make unsupported read-back/drift operations explicit rather than pretending they are available.
value: Prove one-source-of-truth synchronization while creating the extension boundary needed for GitHub, GitLab, Cloudflare, Kubernetes and later providers.
